en_note: Machine translation by Claude (my reading), not on Pesna.org and not checked by a native speaker. Treat it as a study aid.
translator_notes: Traditional revolutionary-era song naming Dame Gruev and Goce Delchev as those who will take over the dying man's horse and gun. 'на мосто' I read as 'on the bridge'; Karamfilo is the one struck.

lines.en: Come on, a gun went off, hey dear,
a gun went off.
Come on, a gun went off, hey dear,
up on the bridge.
Come on, it struck him, hey dear,
it struck him.
Come on, it struck him, hey dear,
Karamfilo.
Come on, he cried out, screamed, hey dear,
cried out, screamed.
Come on, he cried out, screamed, hey dear,
Karamfilo.

lines.lat: Ajde koj ḱe gleda, bre džanam,
lines.en: Come on, who will look after, hey dear,
who will look after.
